required_audit_coverage.name: required_audit_coverage
required_audit_coverage.detail: report covers all 24 Required Audit items with substantive aligned answers
required_audit_items: Is `decision_meta` present, valid, `APPROVED`, and on legal mainline `engineering_branch`?
Does `skill_profiles` use only active skills from `.codex-skills/registry.json`?
Does `codex_execution_report.md` match this decision ID and round ID?
Does `pytest_result.txt` match this decision ID, round ID, and report ID?
Does `execution_log.json` record every required command from command-plan?
Were any omitted or unauthorized commands executed?
Did the implementation avoid modifying forbidden paths?
Did the implementation avoid Web/frontend runtime, runner dispatch, workflow dispatch, model API invocation, database writes, cleanup apply, sample solving, and external reverse tools?
Does post-final sync preserve and compare precise timestamps rather than only truncated timestamp strings?
Does post-final sync record final gate artifact identity, such as path plus SHA-256 or equivalent digest?
Does post-final sync record context packet artifact identity, such as path plus SHA-256 or equivalent digest?
Does `current_context_packet.json.auditor_context` explain the source of `final_gate_status` with current final gate IDs and source artifact identity?
Does the previous warning condition become either absent or explicitly reclassified as non-active when the context packet is source-synced to the current final gate artifact?
Does a genuinely stale context packet still warn or fail in tests?
Does `post_final_evidence_sync_result.json` carry current decision, round, and report IDs?
Does `final_gate_result.json` pass?
Does report-summary match the execution report?
Does run-closeout archive this round if command-plan permits closeout?
Did this round reuse existing post-final sync/context/final-check/report foundations instead of reimplementing them?
Did the final conclusion avoid claiming `ACCEPTED` unless all hard gates and tests support it?
